## Summary
Q3 FY2026 stands out with the lowest EBITDA margin (75.61 USD/t) while Q1 FY2027 recovered to 80.44 USD/t, approaching the best performance in Q2 FY2026 (80.26 USD/t). The dip was driven by lower FOB realizations (104.12 USD/t in Q3 vs. 109.82 USD/t in Q1 FY2027) combined with elevated C1 costs (20.69 USD/t in Q3), and demurrage has been climbing steadily to 0.06 USD/t in Q1 FY2027.

## Root Cause & Action
The Q3–Q4 margin squeeze reflects weaker iron ore pricing (market-driven CFR), while C1 costs remained sticky around 21 USD/t. Demurrage tripled from 0.01 to 0.06 USD/t over five quarters, signaling port bottlenecks or vessel scheduling inefficiencies—though still small, this trend erodes margin and risks contractual penalties.

**Next step:** Conduct a port operations review targeting demurrage triggers (loading delays, berth utilization) and benchmark Q1 FY2027 C1 cost drivers against Q2 FY2026 to lock in efficiency gains.
